questions.stem:
Read the paragraph and choose the best summary:
'The internet has revolutionised the way people communicate. Email, social media, and instant messaging have made it possible to connect with anyone anywhere in the world within seconds. However, this constant connectivity has also led to issues like cyberbullying, misinformation, and the erosion of privacy.'

Best summary:

options.option_text: The internet is harmful and should be regulated more strictly
The internet has transformed communication, bringing both benefits of global connectivity and problems like cyberbullying and privacy loss
Social media is the main cause of cyberbullying in the modern world
Email and messaging apps have made communication faster than ever

questions.explanation: B is correct. A good summary captures the MAIN IDEA of the entire paragraph, not just one aspect. The paragraph discusses: (1) internet's revolutionary impact on communication (2) specific positive tools (3) specific negative consequences. Option B captures all three elements concisely.

questions.stem:
Read and choose the best title:
'Deforestation has become one of the most critical environmental threats of our century. Millions of hectares of forests are cleared annually for agriculture and urban development. This not only destroys the habitat of countless species but also contributes significantly to climate change by reducing the carbon absorption capacity of the earth.'

Best title:

options.option_text: Urban Development and Its Benefits
Deforestation: A Growing Environmental Crisis
Carbon Absorption in Forests
Animal Habitats and Their Importance

questions.explanation: B is correct. The best title reflects the CENTRAL THEME. The paragraph is about deforestation as an environmental crisis — causes (agriculture, urban development) and effects (habitat loss, climate change). 'A Growing Environmental Crisis' captures this broader framing.

questions.stem:
Choose the sentence that BEST summarises the following passage:
'Yoga is an ancient practice that originated in India over 5,000 years ago. It combines physical postures, breathing exercises, and meditation to promote overall well-being. Today, millions of people worldwide practice yoga to reduce stress, improve flexibility, and achieve mental peace.'

options.option_text: Yoga is an Indian tradition that helps people become flexible
Yoga, an ancient Indian practice, promotes physical and mental well-being and is practised globally today
Millions of people do yoga because it helps with stress relief
Ancient Indian practices like yoga have become popular globally

questions.explanation: B is correct. A summary should include: (1) origin (ancient Indian practice), (2) content (physical, breathing, meditation), (3) benefits (well-being, stress, flexibility, peace), (4) reach (global). Option B is the only one that captures all these elements concisely.

questions.stem:
What is the central theme of the following passage?
'Across the world, languages are disappearing at an alarming rate. Linguists estimate that one language dies every two weeks. When a language disappears, an entire cultural heritage, a unique way of viewing the world, and often centuries of oral tradition are lost forever. Preserving endangered languages is therefore not merely a linguistic concern but a humanitarian imperative.'

options.option_text: Linguistics is an important academic field
The rapid extinction of languages represents a significant cultural and humanitarian loss
Oral traditions are more important than written literature
Linguists should study endangered languages before they disappear

questions.explanation: B is correct. The CENTRAL THEME is the larger argument being made. The passage argues: (1) languages are dying fast, (2) each death is a cultural/humanitarian loss, (3) preservation is a humanitarian duty. Option B encapsulates the argument without being too narrow or too broad.

questions.stem:
The passage below is about:
'Meditation has been practised for thousands of years in various cultures. Modern neuroscience now confirms what practitioners have long claimed: regular meditation changes the brain in measurable ways. Studies show that it increases grey matter in areas associated with emotional regulation, reduces the size of the amygdala (the brain's fear and stress centre), and improves focus and concentration.'

The passage is primarily about:

options.option_text: Ancient meditation practices
Scientific evidence for meditation's effects on the brain
The amygdala and its role in stress
How to improve focus through meditation

questions.explanation: B is correct. The paragraph's primary focus is on modern neuroscience confirming meditation's brain-changing effects. While it mentions ancient practice and specific benefits, the central idea is the SCIENTIFIC EVIDENCE for how meditation changes the brain structurally.

questions.stem:
Choose the best one-sentence summary of the following passage:
'The fast food industry has grown dramatically over the past five decades. While it offers convenience and affordability, it has been linked to rising rates of obesity, heart disease, and diabetes. Many public health experts argue that the industry needs stricter regulation to reduce the consumption of unhealthy food, particularly among children.'

options.option_text: Fast food is dangerous and should be banned immediately
The fast food industry's growth has created public health challenges, prompting calls for regulation
Children are the most vulnerable group to fast food addiction
Fast food is convenient and affordable for many people

questions.explanation: B is correct. The summary must reflect: (1) industry growth, (2) health problems caused, (3) proposed solution (regulation). Option B captures all three elements without over-generalising or over-narrowing.

questions.stem:
What can be inferred from the following passage?
'Electric vehicles are gradually replacing conventional cars in many parts of the world. Governments are offering incentives and subsidies to promote their adoption. However, the electricity used to charge these vehicles often comes from fossil fuel power plants, raising questions about their true environmental impact.'

options.option_text: Electric vehicles are worse for the environment than conventional cars
Electric vehicles may not be as environmentally friendly as commonly assumed
Governments should stop subsidising electric vehicles
All electricity should come from renewable sources

questions.explanation: B is correct. INFERENCE = a conclusion drawn from evidence without being explicitly stated. The passage says EVs use electricity from fossil fuels → questions environmental benefit → we can INFER that EVs may not be as green as assumed. This is softer than saying 'EVs are worse' (which is not supported).

questions.stem:
Which title best fits this passage?
'In the modern workplace, soft skills are often valued as much as technical expertise. Employers seek candidates who can communicate effectively, work in teams, adapt to change, and solve problems creatively. While degrees and certifications remain important, the ability to collaborate and lead has become increasingly crucial in today's dynamic job market.'

options.option_text: The Decline of Academic Qualifications
Soft Skills: The New Currency of the Workplace
Why Universities Need to Change Their Curriculum
Technical Skills vs. Communication Skills

questions.explanation: B is correct. The best title captures the CENTRAL THEME creatively. The passage argues soft skills (communication, teamwork, adaptability) are now as valued as technical skills in the workplace. 'Soft Skills: The New Currency' metaphorically captures their growing value without implying technical skills are declining.

questions.stem:
What is the author's VIEW in this passage?
'Water scarcity is rapidly becoming a global crisis. By 2050, it is estimated that more than half the world's population will face water shortages. Yet governments continue to subsidise water-intensive agriculture while failing to invest adequately in water conservation technologies and infrastructure. Without urgent policy changes, this crisis will only deepen.'

options.option_text: Water scarcity is a natural phenomenon that cannot be controlled
Governments are failing to address water scarcity adequately and must urgently change policies
Agriculture should be banned to conserve water
The 2050 prediction about water shortage is inaccurate

questions.explanation: B is correct. The author's VIEW = their position or opinion in the passage. The author: (1) identifies water scarcity as a crisis, (2) criticises government subsidies on water-intensive agriculture, (3) calls for 'urgent policy changes.' The view is that GOVERNMENTS ARE NOT DOING ENOUGH and must act urgently.

questions.stem:
The following passage suggests that:
'Over-reliance on technology has created a generation that struggles with basic tasks without digital assistance. Simple arithmetic, reading maps, and remembering phone numbers have become rare skills. While technology offers incredible conveniences, its excessive use may be stunting cognitive development and independence.'

options.option_text: Technology should be completely eliminated from education
Balanced technology use is important; excessive dependence may harm cognitive skills
Arithmetic and map-reading should be compulsory in schools
Digital tools are superior to traditional learning methods

questions.explanation: B is correct. The passage warns about 'over-reliance' and 'excessive use' — NOT about technology in general. The implicit suggestion is that balanced use is better. 'May be stunting cognitive development' is a warning, and the solution implied is moderation, not elimination.
